newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Poor upkeep said behind Estonia ferry disaster.
newsitem.headline: Poor upkeep said behind Estonia ferry disaster.

text.p: The Estonia ferry disaster which cost 852 lives in 1994 was caused by poor maintenance, faulty loading and excessive speed, an expert group commissioned by the ship's German builders said on Friday.

"We are convinced the reason for the shipwreck is the extremely poor maintenance of the visor and ramp, its locks, hinges and sealings in combination with a faulty allocation of cargo and the too high speed under the prevailing and foreseen weather conditions," lawyer Peter Holtappels, who appointed the group, said in a statement.
The roll-on-roll-off ferry's bow visor snapped off in a Baltic storm in September 1994 and a protective ramp collapsed, sending thousands of tonnes of water onto the car deck.

The German builders, Meyer Werft, set up the group in response to a preliminary report released by a three-nation committee probing the loss of the Estonia southwest of Finland shortly after the accident.

"Already during the first days of October 1994...the international commission released a preliminary report in which it was hinted that the ship went down because of a construction fault," the German group said.

The group said it based its report on witnesses, pictures, videos, neutral experts' statements and information from the three-nation committee or its consultants and experts to ensure the report was unbiased.

The three-nation committee, whose findings could influence law suits brought by survivors and victim's families, has still not published its final report. Its Swedish and Estonian chairmen have resigned and been replaced.
